identification.summary: Lemon Sandstorm is Microsoft's name for an Iran-origin threat actor formerly tracked by Microsoft as RUBIDIUM and also known as Pioneer Kitten [S1]. MITRE ATT&CK tracks it as Fox Kitten (G0117) and describes it as a threat actor with a suspected nexus to the Iranian government. MITRE says it has been active since at least 2017 against entities in the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, Australia and North America [S2][S4][S5]. Its signature is broad exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN appliances (Fortinet, Pulse Secure, Palo Alto), followed by hands-on intrusion that relies largely on open-source and dual-use tools [S2][S5][S6][S10]. Microsoft implicated RUBIDIUM in the Pay2Key and N3tw0rm ransomware campaigns that targeted Israel in late 2020 and early 2021 [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Active since at least 2017, per MITRE ATT&CK and CrowdStrike as summarized by MITRE [S2][S4].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Lemon Sandstorm (formerly RUBIDIUM). Microsoft's naming feed lists RUBIDIUM and PIONEER KITTEN as other names [S1]. MITRE G0117 lists the associated names Fox Kitten, UNC757, Parisite, Pioneer Kitten, RUBIDIUM and Lemon Sandstorm [S2]. The MISP galaxy cluster also lists PARISITE and UNC757 and attributes UNC757 to Mandiant [S10]. Parisite is Dragos's name, and Dragos's reporting focuses on ICS-related targeting [S2][S10]. Vendor clusters overlap but are not guaranteed to be identical; see gaps.

attribution.sponsor: Iran. Microsoft lists the actor's origin as Iran and calls RUBIDIUM 'Iran-linked' [S1][S3]. MITRE ATT&CK and CrowdStrike, as summarized by MITRE and MISP, describe a suspected nexus to the Iranian government [S2][S4][S10]. The sources gathered do not name a specific Iranian government organization as sponsor.
attribution.confidence: Microsoft attributes the Pay2Key and N3tw0rm ransomware activity to RUBIDIUM in its 2021 Digital Defense Report coverage, but publishes no confidence level [S3]. MITRE and CrowdStrike use 'suspected nexus' wording, which is lower than a firm state attribution [S2][S4][S10]. CISA's 2020 alert described an 'Iran-based' actor, as cited by MITRE [S6][S2]. The government advisory text was not opened for this record.
attribution.basis: Microsoft threat intelligence and naming taxonomy [S1][S3]; MITRE ATT&CK procedure mapping drawn from ClearSky, CrowdStrike, CISA, Check Point and Fortinet reporting [S2][S4][S5][S6][S7][S8][S9]; MISP galaxy cluster drawn from CrowdStrike and Dragos [S10].

objectives: Gaining and maintaining access to entities that hold sensitive information of likely intelligence interest to the Iranian government, per CrowdStrike's description as carried in the MISP galaxy [S10]. ClearSky called the campaign 'espionage-offensive' [S5]. In 2020-2021 the actor's activity extended to disruptive or financially framed ransomware (Pay2Key, N3tw0rm) against Israeli targets [S3][S7][S8].

sectors: ICS-related entities (per Dragos, as cited in MISP) [S10]
Critical infrastructure in the Middle East (2025 Fortinet incident report, as cited by MITRE) [S9][S2]
targeting.notes: Targeting is driven mainly by exposure of vulnerable internet-facing VPN and remote-access appliances, not by sector alone [S2][S5][S6]. Sector and region lists come from MITRE's group description [S2]. Microsoft separately reported that Iranian actors in general targeted Israeli logistics and maritime firms in the same period; that statement is not attributed specifically to RUBIDIUM [S3].

capabilities.summary: Initial access comes through exploitation of known vulnerabilities in Fortinet, Pulse Secure and Palo Alto VPN appliances and other remote services, including RDP brute forcing [S2][S5][S6][S7]. Persistence relies on web shells (including China Chopper), scheduled tasks, locally created administrator accounts and the sticky-keys accessibility backdoor [S2][S6][S7]. For command and control and tunneling the actor uses ngrok, the custom SSHMinion tool, the FRPC and Go Proxy reverse proxies, PuTTY/Plink and AWS-hosted C2. MITRE also associates the SystemBC proxy malware with the group, citing a 2025 Fortinet incident report [S2][S4][S6][S7][S9]. Credentials are harvested from LSASS dumps, NTDS via Volume Shadow Copy, KeePass databases and credential files [S2][S6]. Collection draws on network shares, local documents, cloud storage and Microsoft Teams, with 7-Zip used for staging [S2][S6]. In 2020 the actor deployed Pay2Key ransomware and used Keybase and Twitter accounts to communicate with victims [S2][S7][S8]. MITRE lists 41 techniques and 5 software entries for G0117 [S2].

campaigns.name: Earliest reported activity
campaigns.summary: MITRE and CrowdStrike place the start of the actor's activity in at least 2017.

campaigns.name: Fox Kitten: widespread Iranian espionage-offensive campaign (ClearSky)
campaigns.summary: ClearSky reports a campaign that exploited known VPN vulnerabilities (Fortinet, Pulse Secure, Palo Alto) and remote services for initial access across multiple countries; MITRE uses this report as a core reference for the group.

campaigns.name: Who Is PIONEER KITTEN? (CrowdStrike)
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike profiles PIONEER KITTEN, including VPN exploitation and tunneling with ngrok and the custom SSHMinion tool.

campaigns.name: CISA AA20-259A: Iran-based actor exploits VPN vulnerabilities
campaigns.summary: CISA alert, as cited by MITRE, describes VPN exploitation followed by web shells, reverse proxies, credential dumping, and collection from shares, cloud storage and Microsoft Teams.

campaigns.name: Pay2Key ransomware campaign
campaigns.summary: Check Point (2020-11-06) and ClearSky (2020-12-17) report Pay2Key ransomware attacks; ClearSky attributes the campaign to Fox Kitten. Microsoft says RUBIDIUM was implicated in Pay2Key attacks targeting Israel.

campaigns.name: N3tw0rm ransomware campaign
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says RUBIDIUM was implicated in the N3tw0rm ransomware campaign that targeted Israel in late 2020 and early 2021.

campaigns.name: Middle East critical infrastructure intrusion (Fortinet incident response)
campaigns.summary: Fortinet reports an Iranian intrusion into strategic Middle East critical infrastructure; MITRE cites the report to associate SystemBC with the group. The report's own attribution wording was not reviewed.

diamond.adversary: Iran-origin actor with a suspected Iranian government nexus; Microsoft Lemon Sandstorm (formerly RUBIDIUM) [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.capability: Exploitation of n-day VPN and remote-access vulnerabilities; web shells; open-source tunneling and proxy tools (ngrok, FRPC, Go Proxy, Plink, SSHMinion); credential dumping; SystemBC; Pay2Key ransomware [S2][S4][S6][S7][S9].
diamond.infrastructure: Tunnels and reverse proxies from victim hosts to actor C2, including ngrok and AWS-hosted C2. Keybase and Twitter accounts were used for ransomware victim communication [S2][S7].
diamond.victim: Oil and gas, technology, government, defense, healthcare, manufacturing and engineering entities in the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, Australia and North America; Israeli organizations hit by ransomware in 2020-2021 [S2][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Access to information of intelligence interest to the Iranian government [S10], and ransomware operations against Israel during a period Microsoft describes as escalating Iran-Israel tensions [S3].
diamond.technology: Unpatched internet-facing VPN appliances (Fortinet, Pulse Secure, Palo Alto) and exposed RDP; Windows Active Directory environments; collaboration and cloud storage including Microsoft Teams [S2][S5][S6].

gaps: Primary documents were not opened in this session; their content is taken from MITRE ATT&CK's STIX procedure descriptions and the MISP galaxy. These include CrowdStrike 'Who Is PIONEER KITTEN?', ClearSky's Fox Kitten and Pay2Kitten reports, CISA AA20-259A, Check Point's Pay2Key alert, the Fortinet 2025 incident report and Dragos PARISITE (the hosts were blocked or unreachable).

Web search was unavailable for this run because the shared search budget was exhausted. Reporting after 2021 is therefore thin. That includes any 2024 US government advisory on Iran-based actors cooperating with ransomware affiliates and access brokering, and any 'Br0k3r' or 'xplfinder' persona; these were not verified and are not included here.

ZDNet reporting on the sale of network access on underground forums and an FBI flash on F5 device exploitation appears in the imported references, but could not be opened. Access-brokering claims are therefore not included.
Microsoft has no public Lemon Sandstorm actor profile or dedicated blog post that could be found; Microsoft coverage here is limited to the naming taxonomy and the 2021 MDDR blog [S1][S3].

Cluster boundaries: Parisite (Dragos), UNC757 (Mandiant) and Fox Kitten/Pioneer Kitten (ClearSky/CrowdStrike) are mapped together by MITRE and MISP [S2][S10]. No vendor statement confirming full equivalence with Lemon Sandstorm was reviewed. Microsoft's own mapping lists only RUBIDIUM and PIONEER KITTEN [S1].
The specific Iranian sponsoring organization (for example IRGC or MOIS) is not stated in any source gathered.
The 2025 Fortinet report's own attribution language and the victim's identity are unverified; MITRE uses it only to support the SystemBC association [S2][S9].
ICS targeting rests on the MISP summary of Dragos reporting; the specific ICS victims and any OT impact are unverified [S10].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (OE): Internet-facing VPN concentrators, remote-access gateways and exposed RDP are key cyber terrain. The actor's entry depends on known, patchable flaws in Fortinet, Pulse Secure and Palo Alto appliances [S2][S5][S6]. Defense, government, oil and gas, and engineering networks in CENTCOM-, EUCOM- and NORTHCOM-relevant regions fall within its reported victimology [S2]. STEP 2 (effects): Public disclosure of VPN CVEs gives this actor a wide target set. Delayed patching on mission-partner and DIB networks widens exposure, and the actor's use of legitimate tunneling tools blends with administrative traffic [S2][S6]. STEP 3 (adversary template): VPN n-day exploitation; then web shell or local admin account; then scheduled-task reverse proxy (FRPC, ngrok, SSHMinion, SystemBC); then credential dumping (LSASS, NTDS, KeePass); then RDP/SMB lateral movement; then collection from shares, cloud storage and Teams. Ransomware is optional, as with Pay2Key [S2][S4][S6][S7][S9]. STEP 4: MLCOA is persistent access to defense, government and energy networks for collection of interest to Iran [S2][S10]. MDCOA is a pivot from long-held access to ransomware or disruptive effects against partner-nation critical infrastructure during a regional crisis. Candidate indicators: Pay2Key against Israel [S3][S7] and the 2025 Middle East critical-infrastructure intrusion [S9]. Further candidate indicators: new scheduled tasks with legitimate-looking names such as 'lpupdate'; binaries named svhost or dllhost in unusual paths; outbound ngrok or FRP connections; new local administrator accounts; and VSS-based NTDS access after VPN logins from unfamiliar sources [S2][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: JCC2 views should track patch and compromise-assessment status of internet-facing VPN appliances across the DODIN and mission partners. Exploitation of known VPN CVEs is this actor's primary entry vector, and patching alone may not evict an actor already installed [S2][S6]. (2) Authorities: Activity spans espionage and ransomware [S3][S7]. Response may involve DC3, FBI and CISA coordination, and possibly treatment as a criminal incident. Clarify lead-agency roles early, especially for DIB victims. (3) Mission assurance: Ransomware deployment after long-term access threatens availability. Prioritize offline backups and segmentation for mission-critical and ICS-adjacent systems [S7][S9][S10]. (4) Coordination: Share VPN-exploitation and tunneling indicators with coalition partners in the Middle East and Europe, who appear in the actor's victimology [S2]. Track vendor aliases (Pioneer Kitten, Fox Kitten, Parisite, UNC757) so partner reporting is linked to the same cluster [S1][S2].
